correctness.rationale: For every finite connected simple d-regular bipartite graph with 0<mu<d and r>=3, the spectral reflection symmetry confines nontrivial eigenvalues to [mu,2d-mu] plus 2d. Small gains are strictly dominated. The exact compression identity f(u)f(v)-f(1)f(uv)=h(1-h)(1-u)(1-v) bounds every product at mu by rho^(r-1)(1-h-hB) while the 2d mode has magnitude B. Balancing gives B_r. The constructed r-1 full-neighbor stages plus one correction are bounded on every remaining eigenmode by B_r. Strict equality proves the unique multiset. Standalone verify.py passed 326741 exact-rational check calls including graph characteristic polynomials and matrix products. All infinite cases are proved analytically, not by finite checks.

originality.rationale: The original part is the sharp r>=3 common-scalar stochastic finite-horizon minimax on all connected noncomplete regular bipartite graphs and uniqueness of the one-correction multiset. Public 2-step, generic finite-time existence, and unconstrained polynomial-filter results do not imply it. value.rationale: For arbitrary r>=3 on every noncomplete connected regular bipartite graph, an r-parameter nonconvex spectral minimax collapses to an explicit correction and r-1 maximally neighbor-averaging rounds. The graph family includes even cycles, hypercubes and bipartite expanders. Each intermediate matrix is stochastic/nonnegative, a real operational constraint not met by generic Chebyshev polynomials. The strict uniqueness, finite-horizon exact optimum, and comparison with all repeated gains provide a structural and implementable improvement, not a fixed small case or arbitrary table.
